source: M. Denison, '1st AIAA CFD Transition Modeling and Prediction Workshop: OVERFLOW Results for the SST and Langtry-Menter Models' (file: sa-ai/references/overflow_tmw.pdf), Figure 11, PDF page 9
condition: NLF(1)-0416 airfoil, M = 0.2, Re = 4e6, Tu = 0.15%, alpha sweep -4 to 8 deg; OVERFLOW, SST + Langtry-Menter (gamma-Re_theta) transition model, fine grid
notes: Figure 11 is a raster (1280x960 px) embedded image; extracted at native resolution and digitized by color/shape segmentation (scipy.ndimage). Calibration from detected axis tick-mark pixel positions: x_tr/c=0.1 at px 154.5 to 0.8 at px 1221.5 (152.43 px per 0.1, 8 evenly spaced ticks); cl=1.5 at py 113.5 to -1.0 at py 836.5 (144.6 px per 0.5). Only one LM variant is plotted ('Fine grid upper side' blue down-triangles, 'Fine grid lower side' red up-triangles). Because cl is a single global value per run, the small (~0.008) cl split between the raw blue/red marker centroids (an erosion/triangle-orientation artifact) was removed by assigning each alpha the blue-red midpoint cl; xtr is unbiased (left-right symmetric markers). The 7 simulation points correspond to integer-ish alpha steps over the sweep. experiment_* = Somers measurements (open circles upper side, filled circles lower side). Per the caption, the experiment gives TWO points per lift value: the last probed position with laminar flow and the first probed position with turbulent flow (bounds bracketing transition) - hence the pairs at each cl; both bounds are retained here, sorted by cl. The two topmost lower-surface pairs (cl~1.72/1.76) partially overlapped at the image edge and were split geometrically (cl uncertainty ~0.02 for those four points only).
